name: Omaphones
author: Jacek Becela
description: JBL, Sony, Nothing, Soundcore and Xiaomi headphones in the bar: battery and noise control, one icon per connected set. Earbuds show left, right and case levels; over-ear sets one figure. Off / ANC / Ambient switching, the ambient level on Sony and Soundcore, ANC strength and low latency on Nothing, and the A2DP codec where PipeWire offers a choice. Any other headphones with Google Fast Pair or a BlueZ battery get the battery meter.

schema.label: Device name or address contains
schema.description: Leave empty to show every connected audio device; set a substring to follow only the matching ones.

schema.label: Read battery over Google Fast Pair
schema.description: Left, right and case levels over the Fast Pair channel. Off: BlueZ's single figure only, and no JBL noise control — its BLE address is announced on this channel. Sony is unaffected.

schema.label: Noise control (ANC / Ambient)
schema.description: The MODE row: Off / ANC / Ambient, following changes made on the device too — plus the ANC strength and the low-latency switch on Nothing. Works on Sony MDR v2 headsets, Nothing earbuds and headphones, Xiaomi Buds 5 Pro, and some JBL earbuds (JBL needs Fast Pair above). Hidden when the device answers for none.

schema.label: Show a percentage instead of the drawn meters
schema.description: On: the lower earbud's percentage next to the glyph, taking a second bar slot. Off: the levels fill the two halves of one drawn mark. A vertical bar always draws the mark.

schema.label: Hide the widget while nothing is connected
Send a notification at the low battery threshold
